BEGIN RID PROTOCOL  

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Identification strategy  
• Event–study / matched-sample difference-in-differences.  
• For each AAER firm (“target”) and its pre-selected control firm we estimate market-model abnormal returns (AR) and cumulate them into CARs around the first public revelation of misconduct (event date = first public announcement).  
Directional hypothesis (H1)  
H1:  SEC-targeted firms suffer economically large and statistically significant stock-price losses at the revelation of misrepresentation. Formally:  
(a) Mean CAR(−1,+1) for targets < 0.  
(b) Mean CAR(−1,+1) for targets is < CAR of matched controls.  
(c) Larger (more negative) CARs are associated with larger subsequent monetary penalties.  

I will not change this hypothesis after Step 1.  

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE (exactly five)  
Spec 1 Target-only event-study mean test  
 CAR_ij(−1,+1) = Σ AR_ij,t , t = −1…+1.  
 Test: H0: E[CAR] = 0 (one-sample t-test).  

Spec 2 Matched-pairs difference in CAR(−1,+1)  
 ΔCAR_i = CAR_target,i − CAR_control,i.  
 Test: H0: E[ΔCAR] = 0 (paired t-test).  

Spec 3 Target-only CAR(−10,+10) mean test (robustness to wider window).  

Spec 4 Matched-pairs difference in CAR(−10,+10).  

Spec 5 Cross-sectional OLS: log(TotalPenalties_i) = α + β·(−CAR_i(−1,+1)) +  
  controls(Size, Leverage, ROA, M/B) + ε_i.  
 Prediction: β > 0 (larger price drops ⇒ larger penalties).  

No other specifications will be run.  

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
I will reject H1 if EITHER of the following occurs:  
• Spec 1: mean CAR(−1,+1) ≥ 0 OR p-value > 0.10, two-sided.  
OR  
• Spec 2: mean ΔCAR(−1,+1) ≥ 0 OR p-value > 0.10.  
If either condition is met, the hypothesis fails; otherwise it survives.  

STEP 4 — R CODE (self-contained)

```r
# --- Load packages ---
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(broom)

# --- INPUT DATA ---
# aaer_events: one row per AAER firm with
#  firm_id, event_date (first public announcement), control_id
# crsp_returns: daily returns with
#  permno, date, ret, mkt_ret  (market return = CRSP value-weighted)

# compustat_controls: firm-level covariates for year-t-1
#  firm_id, size=log(at), leverage=lt/at, roa=ib/at, mb=mkvalt/at
# penalties: firm_id, total_penalty_usd

# --- Helper: abnormal returns ---
get_ar <- function(df, event_date){
  est_win <- df %>% 
    filter(date >= event_date - 250 & date <= event_date - 30)
  mm <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est_win)
  df %>% 
    mutate(ar = ret - predict(mm, newdata = .))
}

# --- Build CARs for targets and controls ---
cars <- aaer_events %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(firm_id, control_id), 
               names_to = "role", values_to = "permno") %>%
  left_join(crsp_returns, by = c("permno" = "permno")) %>% 
  group_by(permno, event_date) %>% 
  arrange(date) %>% 
  group_modify(~{
      ar_df <- get_ar(.x, unique(.x$event_date))
      ar_df %>%
        filter(date %between% c(unique(.x$event_date) - 10, 
                                unique(.x$event_date) + 10)) %>%
        summarise(
          CAR_m1_p1  = sum(ar[date %between% c(unique(.x$event_date)-1,
                                               unique(.x$event_date)+1)], na.rm=TRUE),
          CAR_m10_p10 = sum(ar, na.rm=TRUE)
        )
  }) %>% 
  ungroup()

# --- Split targets / controls ---
targets   <- aaer_events$firm_id
cars <- cars %>% 
  mutate(target = permno %in% targets)

# --- Spec 1: target-only mean CAR(−1,+1) ---
spec1 <- t.test(cars$CAR_m1_p1[cars$target==TRUE])

# --- Spec 2: paired diff CAR(−1,+1) ---
paired <- cars %>% 
  group_by(event_date) %>% 
  summarise(delta = CAR_m1_p1[target] - CAR_m1_p1[!target])
spec2 <- t.test(paired$delta)

# --- Spec 3: target-only CAR(−10,+10) ---
spec3 <- t.test(cars$CAR_m10_p10[cars$target==TRUE])

# --- Spec 4: paired diff CAR(−10,+10) ---
paired2 <- cars %>% 
  group_by(event_date) %>% 
  summarise(delta = CAR_m10_p10[target] - CAR_m10_p10[!target])
spec4 <- t.test(paired2$delta)

# --- Spec 5: penalties regression ---
cross <- cars %>% 
  filter(target) %>% 
  select(permno, CAR_m1_p1) %>% 
  left_join(penalties, by = c("permno" = "firm_id")) %>% 
  left_join(compustat_controls, by = c("permno" = "firm_id")) %>% 
  mutate(drop = -CAR_m1_p1, 
         logpen = log1p(total_penalty_usd))
spec5 <- lm(logpen ~ drop + size + leverage + roa + mb, data = cross)
spec5_sum <- summary(spec5)

# --- Output objects ---
list(spec1 = tidy(spec1),
     spec2 = tidy(spec2),
     spec3 = tidy(spec3),
     spec4 = tidy(spec4),
     spec5 = tidy(spec5_sum))
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (expected)  
Because this is a pre-analysis plan, numbers below are expectations, not actual estimates.  

Spec 1 Mean CAR(−1,+1) ≈ −0.12 (-12%), t ≈ −9, p < 0.001.  
Spec 2 Mean paired ΔCAR(−1,+1) ≈ −0.11, t ≈ −8, p < 0.001.  
Spec 3 Mean CAR(−10,+10) ≈ −0.20, t ≈ −10.  
Spec 4 Mean paired ΔCAR(−10,+10) ≈ −0.18, t ≈ −9.  
Spec 5 β̂_drop ≈ 0.80 (s.e. 0.20), p < 0.001.  

Gate assessment  
Both gate conditions (Spec 1 and Spec 2) are expected to show large negative and highly significant effects (p < 0.10). Consequently, the falsification gate would NOT be triggered; H1 would be retained.  

END RID PROTOCOL

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — event dates are (1) first public announcement of potential misconduct and (2) final SEC enforcement action; outcome = cumulative abnormal return around each event date; benchmark = matched-firm adjusted returns

key_variables.control: matched firms on industry, size, book-to-market
key_variables.outcome: cumulative abnormal return (CAR) from CRSP daily returns adjusted for matched-firm returns
key_variables.time_period: event windows of [-1,0], [-1,+1], [-10,+10] around announcement dates

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms lose on average 38% of market value from the misconduct period through final resolution; direct penalties account for only a small fraction (~3%) of total costs — the majority is reputational loss
_ground_truth.main_effect: -38% total market value loss from misconduct revelation through resolution
key_robustness: decomposition of loss into direct penalties vs. reputational

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Disclosure of financial misrepresentation and subsequent enforcement milestones
identification_strategy_detail.event_window: Multiple windows around key enforcement dates (initial disclosure, formal investigation, charges, settlement)
identification_strategy_detail.estimation_window: Pre-event clean period for market model estimation
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: Market efficiently impounds expected costs at each disclosure milestone. Abnormal returns around enforcement events reflect the firm-specific cost of misrepresentation, not confounding news.

key_magnitudes.total_market_value_loss: Average 38% decline in market-adjusted equity value
key_magnitudes.legal_penalty_share: ~8.6% of total loss attributable to legal penalties
key_magnitudes.reputation_loss_share: ~66.6% of total loss attributed to reputation damage
key_magnitudes.expected_legal_penalty_share: ~24.8% of total loss from anticipated but not yet imposed penalties

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Decomposition is robust across subsamples (SEC-only vs DOJ, different time periods). Results hold after controlling for firm size, industry, and severity of misrepresentation.
